name: Alu Vadi
subtitle: colocasia leaves rolled with sweet-sour gram flour paste, steamed and sliced

ingredients.qty: 12 large leaves (alu paan), the leaves not the corm, stems and thick veins shaved flat

ingredients.note: helps the rolls hold when sliced
not optional. The acid is what stops the leaves itching
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak a lime-sized ball of tamarind in 6 tbsp warm water for 20 minutes and squeeze out a thick pulp. Thin, watery tamarind will not do. It is both the flavour and the thing that neutralises the calcium oxalate that makes colocasia itch.
Wash and dry the leaves completely, then shave the raised veins flat with a knife held almost parallel to the leaf so the rolls fold without cracking.
The steamed rolls must cool fully, about 30 minutes, before slicing, or they will fall apart.

steps.text: Mix the besan, rice flour, tamarind pulp, jaggery, chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, asafoetida, 1 tbsp sesame and salt into a thick, spreadable paste, adding water a teaspoon at a time only if it is too stiff.
steps.tip: It should be the consistency of soft butter. Spreadable but not runny, or it will slide out of the rolls while steaming.

steps.text: Lay a leaf shiny side down, tip pointing away from you, and spread a thin, even layer of paste over the whole surface.
Lay a second leaf on top facing the opposite way, spread again, and repeat until you have a stack of 3 leaves.
steps.tip: Alternating the direction of the leaves gives you the spiral pattern when you slice.

steps.text: Fold in both long sides by 3cm, spread paste on the folded edges, then roll from the wide end into a tight cylinder. Seal the end with paste. Make 4 rolls.
Steam the rolls over rolling water 25-30 minutes, until a knife goes through cleanly and the outside is a dull olive green.
Cool completely, 30 minutes, then cut into 1.5cm slices with a sharp thin knife.
Heat 4 tbsp oil in a kadhai and shallow-fry the slices in batches, 2 minutes a side, until the edges crisp and brown.
Heat the remaining oil, pop the mustard seeds with the remaining sesame, and pour over the fried slices.
Finish with fresh coconut and coriander and eat warm.
steps.tip: If your mouth tingles at all, the tamarind was too weak. A squeeze of lemon over the slices fixes it.

storage: Steamed rolls keep 4 days refrigerated and freeze for a month whole; slice and fry from chilled. Fried slices are best eaten within a few hours.
